llm.reply:
The KRAS gene product is a small GTPase [11: "encodes a protein that is a member of the small GTPase superfamily"]. The records describe its activity through family membership and nucleotide-bound states rather than as a formal molecular-function annotation [30: "binding both the active (GTP-bound) and inactive (GDP-bound) forms of KRAS"].

## GTPase Nucleotide Cycling

KRAS switches between an active GTP-bound form and an inactive GDP-bound form [30: "the active (GTP-bound) and inactive (GDP-bound) forms of KRAS"]. A guanine nucleotide exchange factor promotes its activity [28: "the cognate guanosine exchange factor (GEF) Son of Sevenless 1 that drives KRAS"]. Inhibitors can target the protein's switch-II pocket [30: "engages the switch-II pocket through a water-mediated hydrogen-bond network"].

## Oncogenic Activation

A single residue change can make KRAS constitutively active [11: "A single amino acid substitution is responsible for an activating mutation"]. This transforming protein is linked to several cancers [11: "implicated in various malignancies, including lung adenocarcinoma, mucinous adenoma, ductal carcinoma of the pancreas and colorectal carcinoma"]. In colorectal cancer, mutant KRAS acts upstream of a transcription factor [27: "KRAS* activates the transcription factor CP2 (TFCP2)"].

## Isoforms and Targeting

Alternative splicing produces two protein forms [11: "Alternative splicing leads to variants encoding two isoforms that differ in the C-terminal region"]. Covalent drugs currently reach only one oncogenic allele [29: "beyond replacing glycine at position 12 with cysteine (G12C), which is clinically drugged through covalent inhibitors"].

llm.reply:
KRAS encodes a protein that belongs to the small GTPase superfamily [11: "encodes a protein that is a member of the small GTPase superfamily"]. Its OMIM entry is titled KRAS PROTOONCOGENE, GTPase; KRAS [4]. The protein exists in active and inactive nucleotide-bound states that inhibitors can target [30: "binding both the active (GTP-bound) and inactive (GDP-bound) forms of KRAS"].

## Activity and Regulation

A single amino-acid substitution can activate the protein [11: "A single amino acid substitution is responsible for an activating mutation"]. KRAS is driven by a guanine nucleotide exchange factor [28: "the cognate guanosine exchange factor (GEF) Son of Sevenless 1 that drives KRAS"]. The gene symbol is KRAS [1]. The gene name is KRAS [5]. The literature entity name is Kras [6].

## Oncogenic Roles

The transforming protein is linked to several cancers [11: "implicated in various malignancies, including lung adenocarcinoma, mucinous adenoma, ductal carcinoma of the pancreas and colorectal carcinoma"]. In colorectal cancer, oncogenic KRAS reprograms fibroblasts [27: "KRAS* transforms the phenotype of carcinoma-associated fibroblasts (CAF) into lipid-laden CAFs, promoting angiogenesis and tumor progression"]. One paper is titled Oncogenic KRAS Drives Lipofibrogenesis to Promote Angiogenesis and Colon Cancer Progression [9]. KRAS is mutated in most pancreatic tumours [28: "mutated in up to 90% of all pancreatic ductal adenocarcinomas (PDACs)"]. One review is titled Targeting KRAS in pancreatic cancer [14].

## Therapeutic Targeting

KRAS was long considered hard to drug [26: "KRAS has been deemed a challenging therapeutic target, even \"undruggable\""]. A related review is titled KRAS mutation: from undruggable to druggable in cancer [2]. Degraders can remove many mutant forms [29: "potently degrades 13 out of 17 of the most prevalent oncogenic KRAS alleles"]. One paper is titled Targeting cancer with small-molecule pan-KRAS degraders [18]. Another is titled A pan-KRAS inhibitor and its derived degrader elicit multifaceted anti-tumor efficacy in KRAS-driven cancers [22]. Related publications include PMID 34776511 [8]. Another is PMID 37768068 [13]. Another is PMID 38686056 [17]. Another is PMID 39298590 [21]. Another is PMID 40780213 [25].

## Variants and Trials

One ClinVar variant is NM_004985.5(KRAS):c.458ATG[1] (p.Asp154del) [3]. Another is NM_004985.5(KRAS):c.36T>C (p.Gly12=) [10]. Another is NM_004985.5(KRAS):c.337C>T (p.Leu113=) [15]. Another is NM_033360.4(KRAS):c.524A>G (p.Glu175Gly) [19]. Another is NM_004985.5(KRAS):c.417T>A (p.Ile139=) [23]. One trial is Sorafenib in Combination With Irinotecan in Metastatic Colorectal Cancer Patients With KRAS Mutated Tumors [7]. Another is PREMIUM, Observational Study [12]. Another is A Trial of mFOLFIRI With MEK162 in Patients With Advanced RAS (HRAS, NRAS, or KRAS) Positive Metastatic Colorectal Cancers [16]. Another is Frequency of EGFR and KRAS Mutations and Clinical-prognostic Correlation in Brazilian Lung Cancer Patients [20]. Another is A Phase 1/2, Study Evaluating the Safety, Tolerability, PK, and Efficacy of Sotorasib (AMG 510) in Subjects With Solid Tumors With a Specific KRAS Mutation (CodeBreaK 100) [24].
